Minimal integration fix record

Director-Orchestrator repair authority: this minimal-fix lane operates only inside an issued Foreman repair work order. The acting Foreman selects the method, sequence and boundaries before mutation and may approve reuse of the existing diagnosis and focused checks. The compact MINIMAL_FIX record below is supporting evidence, not separate permission to execute. A failed, expanded or uncertain step returns to the Foreman for a revised order; it does not authorize provider reassignment or a substitute fix. Ordinary non-repair assignments retain provider judgment, and other projects retain their own ownership and procedures.

Use only for a trivial, unambiguous, reversible correction whose expected state is already established and whose correctness an existing focused check can prove. Pre-stage at most three conditional attempts. Stop on success; recovery requires temporary failure; a third attempt requires materially new information or a substantially different transport. Never repeat ambiguous paid dispatch. If an attempt expands or requires interpretation, stop and use the normal bounded assignment workflow.

MINIMAL_FIX
Issue: <concise defect>
Classification: <why every minimal-fix eligibility condition is satisfied>
Method: <deterministic_autofix | current_session_micro_fix | batched_minor_fix>
Surface: <exact files, fields, links, identifiers, or integration points>
Change: <one-sentence correction>
Validation: <exact focused check and result>
Authority change: none
Behavioral expansion: none
Candidate: <new exact SHA or artifact digest, if applicable>
Next: <continue assignment, review updated candidate, or escalate>

Do not use this record for architecture, business logic, public APIs, schemas, migrations, authentication, authorization, credentials, privacy, security, dependencies, provider contracts, budgets, permissions, deployment, publication, merge policy, unexplained failures, destructive work, or a serious-safety signal. A changed reviewable candidate invalidates all evidence bound to its predecessor and must continue through fresh independent review, security, CI, and merge gates.
